component.name: Siple
component.summary: SIP softphone with an API for agents

description.p: Siple is a desktop SIP softphone for any standards-based PBX or SIP provider: Asterisk, FreePBX, FreeSWITCH or a hosted service. It handles several accounts and lines, hold, transfers and busy lamps, over TLS with SRTP.
Everything Siple shows and does is also available to scripts and AI agents, through a local JSON-RPC API, the siple-cli command-line client and an MCP server.

ul.li: Several accounts and concurrent lines, call waiting, hold, mute and DTMF
Blind and attended transfer, busy lamp field keys, directed pickup and voicemail lamps
UDP, TCP and TLS with certificate pinning; SRTP; Opus, G.722 and G.711
Live configuration: edit the settings file while Siple runs

description.p: Siple is source-available under the Functional Source License 1.1; each release becomes Apache-2.0 two years after it is published.

screenshot.caption: Two calls: one active, one on hold

ul.li: An account whose network socket stops working gets a new one instead of going silent
Resuming a call right after a hold or failed transfer no longer gets refused
In-app updates: retrying or reinstalling right after a cancel works reliably
A badge shows when an agent is listening to a call or a call is being recorded
Settings and the first-run wizard have a switch to start Siple when you log in
Settings: a switch's explanation sits right under it
Updates are checked about every hour, from siple.app
The tray menu shows the version
Auto-hold in a call between two of your own accounts holds the leg that dialed
Settings: explanations next to switches wrap instead of running off the window
AppImage for Linux (x86_64 and aarch64) that updates itself in place
Linux on ARM: aarch64 tarball and AppImage
After an update, Siple reopens its window if it was open, even when set to start hidden
Plain-language errors: failed registrations, calls, busy lamps and transfers say what went wrong and what to try
Setup links: an administrator can send a link that fills in an account, reviewed before anything is saved
First Flatpak build, in preparation for Flathub
Updated SIP stack: registering over TCP or TLS works with Kamailio registrars, and digest authentication fixes
Store editions tell you about updates; direct downloads can install an update in place after checking its signature
New app icon
Interface polish: aligned field heights, segmented controls, icons instead of text arrows

description.p: First builds for the Mac App Store and the Microsoft Store.

ul.li: First public release: several accounts and lines, hold, transfers, busy lamps, TLS and SRTP
A JSON-RPC control API, siple-cli and an MCP server for agents
Keyboard shortcuts and an update check
